newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Deng death may dampen Singapore stock sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Deng death may dampen Singapore stock sentiment.

text.p: The death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping would likely dampen sentiment on the Singapore stock market on Thursday, but the impact could be limited, dealers and analysts said.
A research director for a Singapore broking house said he expected some negative reaction in Asian markets, including Singapore.

But a dealer at a foreign brokerage said: "Singapore will not be affected that much because Deng's death has no direct relevance." A Singapore bank dealer said Hong Kong stocks traded in Europe overnight had not shown much reaction to the news.
Ahead of the news speculative retail interest had been expected to continue to buoy activity but dealers said it would be centred on Malaysian shares traded over the counter.
"Institutions tend to be more cautious into the corporate reporting season (in March) and might continue to take profit," said a dealer.

On Wednesday. the key Straits Times Industrials Index ended up at a high of 2,246.99, up 17.20 points in active trade of over 434.7 million shares. The UOB OTC index, which tracks mostly Malaysian shares, ended 15.99 points up, at 1,324.23.
